extracted.intended_audience: users of Magma / computational algebraists working with permutation and matrix groups
extracted.subtask_description: Documentation and reference for Magma functions and algorithms for permutation groups, G-sets, systems of imprimitivity, and matrix groups; explains meanings, return values, examples, and algorithmic guidance.

rubrics_metrics.name: Orbit of point x under G (a^G, Orbit(G, x))
rubrics_metrics.description: Orbit of point x under G, returned as a G-set.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use Orbit(G,x) or the notation a^G. Example usages and related orbit functions are documented; orbits are returned as G-sets suitable for further Magma operations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Orbit of set S under G (S^G, Orbit(G, S))
rubrics_metrics.description: Orbit of a set S of points under G, returned as a G-set of subsets of X.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use Orbit(G,S) to obtain the G-set whose elements are the images of S under G.

rubrics_metrics.name: Orbit of sequence Q under G (Q^G, Orbit(G, Q))
rubrics_metrics.description: Orbit of a sequence Q of points under G, returned as a G-set of sequences of points from X.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use Orbit(G,Q) when working with ordered tuples/sequences; results are G-sets of sequences.

rubrics_metrics.name: Orbits(G)
rubrics_metrics.description: Constructs all the orbits of G, returning a sequence Q of G-sets where Q[i] contains the points in the ith orbit of G.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Useful to enumerate orbit decomposition of the natural action; examples show output formatting.

rubrics_metrics.name: IsOrbit(G, S)
rubrics_metrics.description: Returns true if subset S of X is a union of orbits of G (i.e., S is invariant under G).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Test subset invariance under the group action; helpful to check whether S is a G-invariant subset.

rubrics_metrics.name: Stabilizer in G of point x (Stabilizer(G, x))
rubrics_metrics.description: Returns the subgroup G_x consisting of those permutations of G that fix x.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Standard permutation-group stabilizer; used to relate cosets of G_x with the orbit of x (orbit-stabilizer correspondence).

rubrics_metrics.name: Stabilizer in G of set S (Stabilizer(G, S))
rubrics_metrics.description: Returns the subgroup of G fixing the set S setwise.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Applies to sets (G-sets of subsets); used in block/stabilizer computations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Stabilizer in G of sequence Q (Stabilizer(G, Q))
rubrics_metrics.description: Returns the subgroup of G fixing the sequence Q (pointwise or appropriately defined for sequences).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use when working with sequences/tuples in derived G-sets.

rubrics_metrics.name: Transversal(G, H)
rubrics_metrics.description: Given group G and subgroup H, returns (i) indexed set T of elements of G forming a right transversal for G over H and (ii) transversal mapping φ : G → T such that φ(g) = T[i] iff g ∈ H · T[i].
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Principal use: analyze cosets and obtain canonical right-coset representatives and a mapping from G to those representatives; example shows producing canonical coset representatives for stab7.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use of transversal mapping for canonical coset representatives
rubrics_metrics.description: The mapping φ(g) = T[i] selects the canonical representative of the coset containing g (i.e., g ∈ H · T[i]).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Can be used to find which coset sends a given point to another (example: m(c) and Index(t,m(c)) show mapping and coset index).

rubrics_metrics.name: IsConjugate(G, x, y)
rubrics_metrics.description: True if x, y ∈ X are conjugate in G; if true, also returns a conjugating element.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Determines if two elements of the G-set lie in the same orbit and yields an explicit g with x^g = y when true; example shows usage on points.

rubrics_metrics.name: IsConjugate(G, R, S) for k-subsets
rubrics_metrics.description: True if k-subsets R and S of X are conjugate in G; if true, also returns a conjugating element.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use to test conjugacy of subsets (e.g., blocks) under group action; example demonstrates sets {2,4} and {3,6}.

rubrics_metrics.name: IsConjugate(G, P, Q) for sequences
rubrics_metrics.description: True if sequences P and Q, each containing k elements of X, are conjugate in G; if true, also returns a conjugating element.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Applies to ordered tuples; returns explicit conjugator when sequences are in the same orbit of the action on sequences.

rubrics_metrics.name: OrbitAction(G, x)
rubrics_metrics.description: Constructs permutation representation L of G obtained by restricting action of G to x^G. Returns (i) natural homomorphism f : G → L (ii) induced group L (iii) kernel of the action.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use to study induced action on a single orbit; OrbitImage and OrbitKernel return image and kernel respectively; example shows restricting action of bgp to orbit containing 2.

rubrics_metrics.name: OrbitAction(G, S) / OrbitImage(G, S) / OrbitKernel(G, S)
rubrics_metrics.description: As above, but for the union of G-orbits of elements of S. OrbitImage returns the induced group L; OrbitKernel returns kernel of the action.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use to restrict G to action on multiple orbits / invariant subsets; mapping between original points and induced group's standard set can be found by applying homomorphism to sequences.

rubrics_metrics.name: Block (system of imprimitivity) definition
rubrics_metrics.description: For transitive G on X, a non-empty subset B ⊆ X is a block for G if for each g ∈ G either B^g = B or B^g ∩ B = ∅. The sets {B^g : g ∈ G} form a G-invariant partition called a block system (system of imprimitivity).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Trivial blocks are singletons; if no non-trivial block system exists G is primitive. Magma represents a block system as a G-set whose elements are subsets of X.

rubrics_metrics.name: IsPrimitive(G)
rubrics_metrics.description: Returns true if G is primitive (i.e., G has no non-trivial system of imprimitivity on X).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Example: print IsPrimitive(cube) => false. There is also IsPrimitive(G,Y) for general G-sets.

rubrics_metrics.name: IsBlock(G, S)
rubrics_metrics.description: Returns true if set of points S is a block for G.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Example: {2,5} is not a block for cube (IsBlock returns false).

rubrics_metrics.name: MinimalPartition(G : Block := ...)
rubrics_metrics.description: Returns a minimal G-invariant partition (block system). If parameter Block is provided as a set of points, returns a minimal partition in which all elements of Block lie in the same block.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Minimal means non-trivial and no finer non-trivial block system exists; example: MinimalPartition(cube: Block := {2,5}) returns the smallest block system putting 2 and 5 together.

rubrics_metrics.name: MaximalPartition(G)
rubrics_metrics.description: Returns a maximal block system for G (a coarsest non-trivial G-invariant partition).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Works similarly to MinimalPartition but returns a maximal system.

rubrics_metrics.name: MinimalPartitions(G)
rubrics_metrics.description: Constructs all minimal block systems of G, returned as a sequence of G-sets.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Any system of imprimitivity can be expressed as a union of blocks of one of the minimal systems; example shows cube has two minimal block systems.

rubrics_metrics.name: BlocksAction(G, Y)
rubrics_metrics.description: Constructs the homomorphism of G onto the group obtained by the action of G on the blocks of Y. Returns (i) natural homomorphism f : G → L (ii) induced group L (iii) kernel of the action.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use to reduce to action on block system; BlocksImage and BlocksKernel return image and kernel. Example: BlocksAction on first minimal system yields an induced group of order 24 (S4).

rubrics_metrics.name: BlocksImage(G, Y) / BlocksKernel(G, Y)
rubrics_metrics.description: BlocksImage returns the image L of the homomorphism induced by action on blocks; BlocksKernel returns the kernel of that homomorphism.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Useful for inspecting the induced permutation group acting on blocks and its kernel.

rubrics_metrics.name: Kantor-style reduction algorithm (TransitiveReduction / PrimitiveReduction)
rubrics_metrics.description: Algorithmic pattern: use OrbitAction to reduce to a transitive group T, then BlocksAction to reduce to a primitive group P; recurse on kernels/taken centralizers to search for elementary abelian normal subgroups.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Example implementation pSubgroup / TransitiveReduction / PrimitiveReduction / AbelianNormalSubgroup demonstrates use of orbit and blocks actions in structural algorithms (p-core detection).

rubrics_metrics.name: GSet(G, Y, f) — construction of a general G-set
rubrics_metrics.description: Construct a general G-set given Y (set) and f a mapping Y × G → Y representing the action; if Y is closure under f then f must be an action of G on Y.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Allows defining arbitrary additional G-sets to work with different actions without forming homomorphic images explicitly. Example: VSpaceAction constructs action of G on a vector space by mapping between V and natural G-set.

rubrics_metrics.name: GSet(G, S) — derived G-set from S
rubrics_metrics.description: Forms the closure of a derived set S of the natural G-set under G and takes the induced action; returns the derived G-set.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Convenient to construct representations such as flags (point-line pairs) by starting with an element and taking its orbit closure under G (example: flags in PSL(3,4)).

rubrics_metrics.name: Definition of derived set and derived G-set
rubrics_metrics.description: Derived sets: subsets of A, k-subsets, k-sequences, ordered partitions, or subsets of Cartesian products of derived sets. The natural action on X induces action on the G-closure of any derived set of X, making it a derived G-set.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use when building complex G-sets (flags, tuples, etc.) from the natural G-set.

rubrics_metrics.name: Access functions for G-sets (Action, Degree, Group, Set, Support, Labelling)
rubrics_metrics.description: Action(Y) mapping giving action on G-set Y; Degree(G, Y) cardinality of G-set; Group(Y) returns group for G-set Y; Set(Y) returns underlying set; Support(Y) returns support; Labelling(G) indexed set mapping natural G-set to standard {1..n}.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use these elementary accessors to inspect and manipulate G-sets and their associated permutation representations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Orbit(G, Y, y) for general G-sets
rubrics_metrics.description: Forms the orbit of y ∈ Y under G in the G-set Y.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Generalization of Orbit to arbitrary G-sets; example usage given with flags of PSL(3,4).

rubrics_metrics.name: Image(g, Y, y)
rubrics_metrics.description: Constructs the image of y ∈ Y under g ∈ G for action on general G-set Y.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Generalizes point-image computation to arbitrary G-sets; illustrated with flags example.

rubrics_metrics.name: Fix(G, Y) and Fix(g, Y)
rubrics_metrics.description: Fix(G,Y): (context) likely returns fixed points under group? Fix(g,Y) returns action of single element g on Y (example shows cycle notation).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Table lists Fix(G,Y) and Fix(g,Y) among orbit/stabilizer functions; use to determine fixed structures. (Exact semantics follow Magma conventions.)

rubrics_metrics.name: IsPrimitive(G, Y) / Transitivity(G, Y) / IsTransitive(G, Y)
rubrics_metrics.description: Generalized tests of primitivity and transitivity for action of G on G-set Y: IsPrimitive checks for non-trivial block systems on Y; IsTransitive checks transitivity; Transitivity computes degree of transitivity or similar property.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use these to probe action properties on derived G-sets (example: IsPrimitive(G, flags) returned false for flags of PSL(3,4)).

rubrics_metrics.name: IsRegular(G, Y) / IsSemiregular(G, Y)
rubrics_metrics.description: Tests whether action of G on Y is regular (transitive with trivial stabilizers) or semiregular (all point stabilizers are trivial).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use to classify types of actions on G-sets (tables list these predicates).

rubrics_metrics.name: IsTransitive(G, Y, k) / IsSharplyTransitive(G, Y, k)
rubrics_metrics.description: Tests k-transitivity and sharp k-transitivity of action of G on Y.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Useful predicates when analyzing high-transitivity properties of induced actions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Orbits(G, Y)
rubrics_metrics.description: Constructs all G-orbits on the G-set Y.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Generalization of Orbits to arbitrary G-sets; use to find orbit decomposition of derived actions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Stabilizer(G, Y, y)
rubrics_metrics.description: Finds the subgroup of G that fixes y ∈ Y (in the action on the G-set Y).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Generalized stabilizer for arbitrary G-sets; can be compared with stabilizer in induced image via Action(G,Y) examples.

rubrics_metrics.name: IsConjugate(G, Y, y, z)
rubrics_metrics.description: Generalized conjugacy test for elements y,z in a G-set Y; returns conjugacy boolean and possibly conjugator.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Applies to derived G-sets; example shown for flags.

rubrics_metrics.name: Action(G, Y) / ActionImage(G, Y) / ActionKernel(G, Y)
rubrics_metrics.description: Constructs the homomorphism φ : G → G^Y where G^Y denotes the representation of G given by its action on Y; also returns image and kernel. ActionImage returns the image, ActionKernel the kernel.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use to obtain the explicit induced permutation group FG acting on Y, and compare stabilizers between G and FG (example: FGstab@@phi eq Gstab).

rubrics_metrics.name: IsFaithful(G, Y)
rubrics_metrics.description: Returns true if G acts faithfully on the G-set Y (i.e., kernel of Action(G,Y) is trivial).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use to test whether the induced action is injective on group elements.

rubrics_metrics.name: IsAltsym(G) / IsAlternating(G) / IsSymmetric(G)
rubrics_metrics.description: Recognition tests for whether G contains Alt(X), or equals Alt(X) or Sym(X) respectively.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: These functions operate by sampling random elements to test primitivity and other characteristics; if random tests fail, a Schreier algorithm is invoked to compute order definitively. Useful for large-degree rapid detection (example: IsAltsym detected subgroup of Sym(1,000,000) fast).

rubrics_metrics.name: EARNS(G) (elementary abelian regular normal subgroup)
rubrics_metrics.description: Returns the unique elementary abelian regular normal subgroup N of G if one exists, otherwise the trivial group.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Applies to primitive groups with abelian socle; used in affine-type analysis. A corresponding homomorphism AffineAction(G) and its image/kernel (AffineImage/AffineKernel) are available.

rubrics_metrics.name: AffineAction(G) / AffineImage(G) / AffineKernel(G)
rubrics_metrics.description: Constructs the homomorphism and induced action φ : G → G_x when G has an elementary abelian regular normal subgroup; AffineKernel returns same subgroup as EARNS(G).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Used to analyze affine-type primitive groups; example shows extracting H and its factored order and composition factors to identify structure.

rubrics_metrics.name: Socle(G)
rubrics_metrics.description: Returns the socle N of G (product of minimal normal subgroups).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Useful for structure analysis of primitive groups; companion functions include SocleFactors, SocleFactor, SocleSeries, SocleImage, SocleKernel, and MinimalNormalSubgroups.

rubrics_metrics.name: MinimalNormalSubgroups(G)
rubrics_metrics.description: Computes the minimal normal subgroups of G.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Primitive groups have at most two minimal normal subgroups; used when decomposing non-abelian socle into direct product of simple groups.

rubrics_metrics.name: SocleFactors(G) / SocleFactor(G) / SocleSeries(G)
rubrics_metrics.description: SocleFactors returns the sequence [S1, S2, ... , Sr] of simple factors of the socle; SocleFactor returns a single factor; SocleSeries returns a composition series for the socle.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use these to examine structure when socle is a product of isomorphic simple groups (example: tensor product case with many factors).

rubrics_metrics.name: SocleImage(G) / SocleKernel(G)
rubrics_metrics.description: SocleImage returns the group induced by conjugation action of G on socle factors; SocleKernel returns kernel of this action.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Helps determine how G permutes socle factors and to extract G-module structure on socle-kernel when needed (examples show GModule usage).

rubrics_metrics.name: Base and Strong Generating Set (BSGS) — definition
rubrics_metrics.description: A base B for G is a sequence of distinct points from X such that only identity fixes B pointwise. Given a base B of length n, subgroups G(i) are stabilizers of first i-1 base points. A subset S of G is a strong generating set if G(i) = <S ∩ G(i)> for i=1..n.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Most permutation-group algorithms rely on availability of a BSGS; computing BSGS can dominate runtime and different Schreier-Sims variants are appropriate in different situations.

rubrics_metrics.name: BSGS(G)
rubrics_metrics.description: Constructs a base and strong generating set for G using Magma's default algorithm choices.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Default automatic choice; Magma saves constructed BSGS for later reuse.

rubrics_metrics.name: SimsSchreier(G)
rubrics_metrics.description: Constructs a BSGS using the standard Schreier–Sims algorithm.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Mainly appropriate for groups of very small degree (less than 100).

rubrics_metrics.name: SolubleSchreier(G)
rubrics_metrics.description: Schreier algorithm exploiting soluble-group structure, recommended when G is known to be soluble.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Choose when group is soluble to speed up BSGS construction.

rubrics_metrics.name: RandomSchreier(G) and its parameters (Max, Run)
rubrics_metrics.description: Constructs a BSGS by random selection of potential strong generators. No guarantee of correctness; stopping criterion controlled by Max (default 100) and Run (default 20).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Useful when order of G is known (set via AssertAttribute(G,'Order',n)) — then RandomSchreier runs until a group of that order is constructed. Verify(G) can be used to validate the result.

rubrics_metrics.name: ToddCoxeterSchreier(G)
rubrics_metrics.description: Applies Leon–Sims Todd–Coxeter based method to select new strong generators and prove correctness.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Algorithm of choice if RandomSchreier is not applicable and degree lies between ~100 and 10,000.

rubrics_metrics.name: Verify(G)
rubrics_metrics.description: Verifies correctness of a BSGS constructed by RandomSchreier; based on Brown/Cannon/Sims verification ideas and Sims' techniques for simple groups.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Designed for groups of degree in excess of 100,000 to validate probabilistic BSGS results.

rubrics_metrics.name: Classification of matrix groups into three computational classes
rubrics_metrics.description: Matrix groups are divided into: (1) finite matrix groups over a field/euclidean ring with moderate degree and a short orbit (≤ 1,000,000) located by Magma (BSGS approach applicable); (2) matrix groups over finite fields (Aschbacher-based machinery can handle many up to degree ~200); (3) groups where SNF can't be constructed (infinite groups and large-degree finite ones) where only element operations are supported.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This classification guides which computations and algorithms are possible for a given matrix group: BSGS-style stabilizer chains, Aschbacher-classification-based methods, or limited element-only operations.

rubrics_metrics.name: GeneralLinearGroup(n, R) (GL(n,R)) creation semantics
rubrics_metrics.description: Creates a shell structure for GL(n,R) representing parameters of the general linear group; does not construct actual generators unless R is a finite field GF(q), in which case generators are automatically constructed when needed.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Printing or operations that require generators will trigger generator construction for GF(q); for other coefficient rings users must supply generators explicitly.

rubrics_metrics.name: Matrix element construction via sequence coercion and Eltseq/ElementToSequence
rubrics_metrics.description: An element of a matrix group may be created by coercing a row-major sequence of its entries into the group. Eltseq or ElementToSequence decomposes a matrix into the corresponding sequence of ring elements.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Example demonstrates coercion into G5 and Eltseq(g) returning the flat list of entries. Use this to build or decompose matrices programmatically.

rubrics_metrics.name: Identity matrix construction (Identity(G) or G!1)
rubrics_metrics.description: Construct the identity matrix of group G via Identity(G) or the coercion G!1.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Standard way to obtain the multiplicative identity in the matrix group context.

rubrics_metrics.name: Arithmetic on matrices (multiplication, exponentiation, inverse)
rubrics_metrics.description: Standard multiplicative operators (* and ^) apply to matrix group elements; inverse obtained via exponentiation to power -1.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examples show g*h, h*g, g^10, and h^-1; operations obey usual matrix algebra rules subject to group membership/coercibility constraints.

rubrics_metrics.name: Accessing matrix entries and rows (g[i,j], g[i]) and modification guidance
rubrics_metrics.description: Entry (i,j) or row i of a matrix g may be accessed with g[i,j] or g[i]. It is not permitted to modify a matrix by redefining entries directly; to modify, convert to a sequence via Eltseq, mutate the sequence, then coerce back into the group.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Direct in-place modification is disallowed because the result may not be a group element; follow convert-modify-coerce workflow.

rubrics_metrics.name: Compatibility rules for matrix multiplication across groups/spaces
rubrics_metrics.description: Multiplication is possible when matrices are elements of (or coercible into) a common matrix group, or when coefficient rings are compatible and dimensions match; multiplication between matrix groups and matrix rings/spaces is supported in compatible cases (e.g., group acting on a space).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Ensure coercibility and dimensional/coefficent compatibility before attempting multiplication; Magma will allow multiplications in certain mixed contexts as described.
